issue: 'h₁íns sēmi h₁áydʰi' for 'give him half of them': sēmi is an adverb ('half-way, partially', cf. Ved. sāmí), so with no partitive genitive the PIE says 'give them partially'; h₁íns is masc. for gʷṓs 'cattle' (cows usually fem.).
léwbʰeh₂ used as a vocative is the nominative form; the eh₂-stem vocative was *-h₂ / short *-a (Gk νύμφα, Ved. amba).
h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom has the accent on the root; Ved. rajatám is oxytone, so *h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm.
h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom: accent on the root, should be *h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm (Ved. rajatám). Otherwise good, including the formula gʷʰént h₁ógʷʰim.

eweket is malformed: it lacks the labiovelar and the reduplication of *wekʷ- (cf. Gk εἶπε; L–Z ewewkʷet, Hirt ewewekʷet). Also ḱerd as nominative (the nom. is *ḱḗr), the thematic angʰetai in place of the nasal present, ǵʰm̥onm̥ for *(dʰ)ǵʰmónm̥, and old notation without laryngeals or accents (owis, eḱwobʰyos) that clashes with the title item.

'ḱóymōys gʷmént' for 'they come to the household': ḱóymōys is instrumental plural. The goal needs acc. sg. ḱóymom (or at least a dat./loc.). Minor: wewr̥tté plus bare acc. h₁íns for 'be turned towards them' is marginal.
HéHḱuns has the accent on the root; the u-stem adjective is oxytone (Ved. āśú-, Gk ὠκύς), so *HeHḱúns.

The forms are correct in Lehmann–Zgusta 1979 notation, but that notation has no laryngeals or accents (owis for h₂ówis, aǵrom for h₂éǵrom, ebʰuget), which is inconsistent with the rest of the corpus and with the title cae7baa2.
'só h₁íh₂ h₁uként': h₁uként is a 3pl aorist but the subject só is singular. It needs 3sg h₁éwkt, which the next sentence uses (neuter-plural h₁íh₂ is the object, not the subject).
h₃réǵm̥ (acc.) has a short root vowel. The root noun keeps the lengthened grade throughout (Lat. rēgem, rēgis; the engine's own gen. is h₃rēǵés), so *h₃rḗǵm̥.
'kʷís-kʷe h₁n̥gʷnís h₁stés?': h₁stés is 3du 'they two are', but the subject h₁n̥gʷnís is singular, so it needs h₁ésti.
'kʷíd-kʷe dʰrówgʰoh₁ h₁ésti?': dʰrówgʰoh₁ is instr. sg. (or nom. du.), not a nominative subject. It needs dʰrówgʰos, as in the answer that follows.
'dʰǵʰémi Hn̥dʰí' for 'below, in the earth': the main reflex of *Hn̥dʰí (Ved. ádhi) means 'on, over'. 'Below' is *Hn̥dʰér / *nér. The lexicon gloss is suspect.
kʷósmead (abl.) is a non-handbook ending; expected *kʷósmōd (the packet itself has h₁énosmōd and h₁ésmōd). The referent of h₁íh₂ 'them' (neut. pl.) after the singular h₁íd 'it' is unclear.
'ménos h₁íd h₂éǵe' for 'let the mind drive it': h₂éǵe is a 2sg imperative, but the subject ménos is 3rd person, so it needs 3sg h₂éǵetu.
péḱewh₁ (instr.) has full grade in both root and suffix. Expected *péḱwh₁ / *péḱuh₁ (acrostatic) or *pḱwéh₁ (cf. Ved. paśvā́).
ḱlḗm 'I heard' applies Stang's law to the verbal 1sg *ḱléwm̥. No handbook gives this, and it makes the form opaque; *ḱléwm̥ is expected. HéHḱuns also has the accent on the root (*HeHḱúns).
